newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Electrabel too protected, says OECD.
newsitem.headline: Electrabel too protected, says OECD.

text.p: Belgian electricity company Electrabel SA enjoys a privileged status which should be reviewed, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said on Tuesday in a report on the Belgian economy.
"Few other electrical power companies in the OECD area have such extensive market power as Electrabel," the OECD said.

"The competition authorities and regulators may wish to scrutinise this situation with a view to enhancing opportunities for other generators and expanding choice for households and small businesses," it added.
Electrabel is presently trying to lock Belgium's electricity distribution companies into long-term supply contracts in return for a share of five percent of its capital.
But the move has been challenged by European Union anti-trust authorities on the grounds it could hamper competition at a time when the EU is trying to prise open the sector.

European Union competition commissioner Karel Van Miert said earlier on Tuesday that the supply contracts could last up to 15 years but that distributors should be free to source 25 percent of their electricity needs elsewhere after a period of 10 years.
The OECD said a recently adopted EU electricity directive, holding out the hope of greater competition in the sector, would probably not have much impact in Belgium.
"Belgium should therefore undertake more ambitious initiatives that go beyond the requirements of the directive," the OECD said.
